post.caption:
Around 500 submarine cables carry over 95% of all international data, and satellite internet handles a tiny fraction of it. Inside each cable the glass threads are thinner than a hair, wrapped in armour that thins out in deep water. The outages are disappointingly physical: ship anchors, dragged fishing gear, earthquakes and undersea landslides, well over a hundred faults a year. Repair ships find the break and haul the cable up to splice it.
